requirements.requirement: Join node1, node2, and node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
requirements.summary: All three nodes joined via rabbitmqctl join_cluster and cluster_status repeatedly shows all three as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with no partitions, both immediately after clustering and after the later node-loss/restart tests.
add_vhost payments succeeded and list_vhosts confirms the vhost exists alongside the default vhost.

requirements.requirement: Create an application account that can publish and consume in the payments vhost
requirements.summary: app_svc user was created with full .*./.*./.*. permissions scoped to the payments vhost, and was directly used (not just configured) to publish and retrieve messages via rabbitmqadmin, proving actual publish/consume capability.

requirements.requirement: Messages published to a durable queue must survive the loss of any one node and remain consumable from the remaining nodes
requirements.summary: A durable quorum queue 'orders' was declared and mirrored across all three nodes. Two messages were published before node3 was stopped (systemctl stop). While node3 was down, the queue still reported both messages present on the surviving 2-node cluster and they were successfully retrieved with their original payloads intact. Node3 was then restarted, rejoined the cluster, and the queue returned to 3 members. This shows the full baseline -> disruption -> consumption during disruption -> recovery cycle.

overall_summary: The executor successfully formed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster, created the payments vhost and an app_svc account with publish/consume permissions on it (demonstrated in practice, not just configured), and ran a genuine bounded node-loss test on a durable quorum queue that showed messages surviving node3's outage and remaining consumable from the two-node remnant, followed by node3's recovery and rejoin. Separately, the executor also completed a full node-restart evidence cycle for all three managed nodes (pre-restart boot id and health, reboot acknowledgement, distinct post-reboot boot id, and recovered RabbitMQ/cluster/queue state), which cross-checks cleanly against the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Hygiene issues are minor: a few residual temp files and a broader-than-strictly-needed 'management' tag on the app account, with no destructive or unrecoverable mutations.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) at all lifecycle phases, so package-manager consistency cannot be independently confirmed beyond the successful yum install output in the executor timeline.

The rabbitmqadmin download command (cmd-e87321261a084186) returned exit code 127 from the trailing python3 --version check; the actual curl/chmod portion appears to have succeeded based on later successful rabbitmqadmin invocations, but the exact success of each sub-command in that chained line cannot be independently isolated from the captured output.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were directly necessary for cluster bring-up, vhost/user provisioning, the node-loss durability test, firewall opening for RabbitMQ ports, and the separate full-node restart protocol (all reversed cleanly: node3 was stopped and restarted, all three nodes rebooted and recovered with distinct post-reboot boot ids consistent with the fixed after_executor snapshot). A few low-risk residues were left behind and not cleaned up: /tmp/rabbitmqadmin (downloaded CLI helper) and /tmp/install.log /tmp/install.pid (background yum install artifacts) persist on the nodes per the after_executor temp-file listing; these are harmless but were not removed. The app_svc account was also tagged 'management' (cmd-82db83085d6c4829), granting management UI/API access beyond the minimum needed for publish/consume, a modest scope-widening rather than a security break. An early /etc/hosts update attempt (cmd-009d1f903e914b6f) was a no-op due to a grep matching the existing 127.0.1.1 entry, requiring a corrective follow-up (cmd-6bd488b5d018425f); this was a logic slip rather than a harmful mutation. No failed services, broken packages, or weakened security controls were observed in the after_executor snapshot (failed-services empty on all nodes, package-health checks simply timed out and are inconclusive rather than showing damage).
